title: How early should you arrive at Heathrow Airport?
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: The sun rising behind planes on the stands, seen through the tall windows of a Heathrow terminal
intro: About two hours before a short-haul flight and three hours before long-haul is the usual advice at Heathrow. Here's how to work out your timing for each terminal, with the 2-litre liquids rule, drop-off and the trains.
seo_description: About 2 hours before short-haul and 3 before long-haul. Heathrow terminals, the 2-litre liquids rule, the £7 drop-off charge and the fastest trains.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Short-haul, bags to drop:** about 2 hours
- **Long-haul:** about 3 hours
- **Hand luggage, Europe:** 90 mins to 2 hours
- **School holidays:** add 30 minutes

This is the timing most airlines and travel guides suggest for Heathrow, checked in November 2026. Your airline's bag drop and gate deadlines are the ones that count, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so check Heathrow's and your airline's current advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Which terminal?
sections.text:
Heathrow has four passenger terminals: 2, 3, 4 and 5. Your terminal is on your booking, and it decides which station, drop-off zone and car park you need.

- **Terminal 5** is mainly British Airways.
- **Terminals 2 and 3** sit next to each other in the middle of the airport, a short walk apart.
- **Terminal 4** is on its own on the south side.

Watch out: British Airways also flies some routes from Terminal 3, and airlines do move. Check the terminal on your booking the day before, not from memory of your last trip.

If you end up at the wrong one, the Elizabeth line and Heathrow Express run free between the terminals, but allow at least 20 to 30 minutes for the change.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City break, hand luggage only | Midweek, mid-morning | **90 minutes to 2 hours** before |
| Sun holiday, bags to drop | 7am in August | **2½ hours** before |
| Long-haul, bags to drop | Evening | **3 hours** before |
| Christmas trip, bags to drop | Mid-December weekend | **3 hours** before |

The extra time on long-haul flights isn't for security. Check-in and bag drop close earlier, and some routes have document checks at the desk, for example for visas or the US ESTA.

sections.heading: Security and the 2-litre liquids rule
sections.image_alt: A busy departure lounge at Heathrow with rows of seats, departure screens and shops on two floors
sections.image_caption: Once you're through security, check the screens for your gate, which can be a long walk away.
sections.text:
Since January 2026, all four Heathrow terminals have new scanners. You can now carry liquids in containers of up to 2 litres in your hand luggage, and keep liquids and laptops in your bag as it goes through. There's no need for the clear plastic bag.

Tip: pack for the strictest airport on your trip, not Heathrow. Many airports abroad still use the 100ml limit, so a 1-litre bottle of sun cream may get through at Heathrow and be taken off you on the way home.

Security queues are usually short outside the peaks. The busiest times are the first wave of short-haul flights in the early morning and the start of the school holidays.

sections.heading: Bag drop and the gate
sections.text:
If you're checking a bag, work back from the bag drop deadline, not the departure time. Most airlines close bag drop about 45 to 60 minutes before a short-haul flight and an hour or more before long-haul. The exact time is on your booking, and the desk won't reopen.

The walk to the gate can be long, especially in Terminal 5, where some gates are in satellite buildings reached by a short underground train. Allow 15 to 20 minutes from security to the gate. Gates usually close 15 to 30 minutes before departure.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.image_alt: A London Underground train pulling into a platform, with a red roundel and brick walls
sections.image_caption: The Piccadilly line is the cheapest way to Heathrow, but the slowest from central London.
sections.text:
- **Heathrow Express:** non-stop from Paddington in about 15 minutes to Terminals 2 and 3, a few minutes more to Terminal 5. The quickest and priciest option.
- **Elizabeth line:** from central and east London to all terminals, with no change. Usually the best balance of price and speed.
- **Piccadilly line:** the Tube, to all terminals. Cheapest, but slow from central London, so allow about an hour.
- **Coaches:** National Express runs to Heathrow from across the country, handy for early flights.

Check for engineering works at weekends, when lines sometimes close and replacement buses add a lot of time.

sections.heading: Dropping off and parking
sections.text:
- **Drop-off charge:** £7 every time a car enters a terminal drop-off zone, from 1 January 2026.
- **Time limit:** a 10-minute maximum stay.
- **Paying:** online by 11.59pm the next day, or you'll get a penalty notice.
- **Free alternative:** drop off at a long stay car park and take the shuttle bus, which adds time.
- **Parking:** booking ahead is almost always much cheaper than turning up.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Heathrow?
sections.text:
Heathrow flies almost everywhere. For long-haul, look at [New York](/destinations/new-york) or [Dubai](/destinations/dubai). For a short break, try [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam), [Rome](/destinations/rome) or [Madrid](/destinations/madrid). Browse the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page, or our [where to go in December](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december) ideas for winter.

If your family can't agree, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's picks into a draw.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Heathrow for an international flight?
faqs.answer: About two hours before a short-haul flight to Europe, and about three hours before a long-haul flight. Allow more at Christmas and the start of the school holidays.

faqs.question: Can you take 2 litres of liquid through Heathrow security?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since January 2026, all four Heathrow terminals allow liquids in containers of up to 2 litres. Check the rules at the airport you're flying back from, as many still use 100ml.

faqs.question: How much is drop-off at Heathrow?
faqs.answer: £7 each time a car enters a terminal drop-off zone, from 1 January 2026, with a 10-minute maximum stay. Pay online by 11.59pm the next day.

faqs.question: Which terminal does British Airways use at Heathrow?
faqs.answer: Mostly Terminal 5, but some British Airways flights use Terminal 3. Check your booking.
